Exposure (bold): her regalia opens to show skin — bare shoulders and arms between pauldron and bracer, a deep open neckline under the gorget with natural cleavage, a high slit in the tabard or robe showing the thigh; armor pieces stay on and symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: the blue underground kingdom of the kobolds: deep silver-mine galleries full of goblin mischief, where rose-pink cobalt-bloom crystals crust the walls and lanterns sputter in poisonous fumes, a glasshouse where the ore melts into glass of the deepest blue, a porcelain palace whose white walls are painted all over in cobalt blue.

Light: natural daylight or the world's own magical glow.

One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Co) and atomic number (27) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
